newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom $1.5 bln U.S. corp bond deal to set tone.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom $1.5 bln U.S. corp bond deal to set tone.

text.p: A large debt offering by WorldCom Inc on Wednesday is likely to set the tone for the U.S. corporate bond market following yesterday's Federal Reserve interest rate hike, said market players.
WorldCom, a large U.S. telephone company, is preparing to sell $1.5 billion in senior notes via Salomon Brothers Inc.

The deal will consist of $300-$400 million seven-year notes with price talk of 80-85 basis points over Treasuries; $700-$800 million ten-year notes with price talk of 93-95 basis points over; and $300-$400 million 30-year bonds putable in the twelfth year with price talk in the mid-90s.
The offering of Ba1/BBB-minus-rated debt is the first since WorldCom purchased MFS Communications Inc last year.
"If this deal goes well, it could give the market a bit of confidence, and if not, the market will be a bit concerned about supply coming out," said one syndicate official.
But another official said no matter what the outcome of the WorldCom deal, the new issue market would be sluggish and unsettled until March employment numbers come out on April 4.
"Everyone will on pins and needles until the employment report because it will show if we are likely to see more Fed tightening."
"Once you have the slate cleared, then you could see issuance pick up during the week of April 7," he added.
Other high-grade debt deals expected for Wednesday are:

-Millipore Corp's offering of $100 million in five-year debt and $100 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities. Price talk is 55 basis points over Treasuries for the five-year tranche and 75 basis points over for the ten-year tranche, market sources said.
-Conseco Inc's offering of $300 million in 30-year bullet capital securities via Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette.
The new issue market for junk bonds is expected to continue at a steady pace over the next several weeks.
But market sources said the Fed's rate increase will make the market for zero coupon and lower credit-quality deals even less friendly environment.
Del Monte Foods is expected to sell $215 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes on Wednesday in connection with a leveraged buyout of the company by Texas Pacific Group, said market sources.
Price talk on the B-minus-rated notes is 10 percent to 10.25 percent, market sources said.
Other junk deals expected for Wednesday include a $165 million offering from Cross Timbers Oil Co via Merrill Lynch & Co and a $120 million deal from Continental Global Group Inc via DLJ.
Corporate bond players said yesterday's negative bond market reaction to the Federal Reserve's move has made the outlook for the new issue market less certain.

While most market players had expected the Fed to hike rates by 25 basis points on Tuesday, many were caught off-guard by comments made by the Fed that suggested additional interest rate hikes may follow.
